title: Make an SDDC LCM component upgrade safe to retry
prompt:
Implement the `sddclcm` package of the `vcf/lcm` Go module. It drives the two VCF 9.1 SDDC LCM operations pinned in `docs/contract.json`: `performComponentAction` with `action=apply`, and `getTask`. Keep the exported API that `sddclcm/sddclcm.go` already declares and use only the Go standard library.

Applying a component upgrade mutates the fleet, so the submission has to be safe to re-send: a lost or 5xx response must never leave a second upgrade running. `ApplyComponentUpgrade` encodes the `ComponentUpgradeSpec` once and then sends those exact bytes on every attempt under one unchanging `X-Correlation-Id`, taken from `UpgradeSpec.CorrelationID`. An empty `CorrelationID` is refused with `ErrMissingCorrelationID` before anything reaches the wire, because such a submission could not be replayed. Retry only transport failures and HTTP 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, up to the configured attempt cap; any other 4xx is final and must not be re-sent. Options `WithHTTPClient`, `WithMaxAttempts`, `WithRetryBackoff` and `WithPollInterval` override the documented defaults, and `NewClient` rejects an empty base URL or bearer token.

The apply request is a POST to `/v1/components/{componentId}` with the path segment percent-encoded and the query exactly `action=apply`. It carries `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `X-Correlation-Id`. Its body is compact JSON with no trailing newline, whose members appear in the ascending `order` given for each schema in `docs/contract.json`. Every optional member that the caller left unset — including an optional map or slice that is present but empty — is omitted entirely rather than sent as `null`, `""`, `[]` or `{}`. `performBackup` is not optional: whenever `lcmPlatformSpec` is sent, `false` is a value that must appear. A 202 yields the accepted `Task`.

`GetTask` is a GET of `/v1/tasks/{taskId}` with a percent-encoded path segment. It carries `Accept` and `Authorization`, but no request body or `Content-Type`, and expects 200. `ApplyUpgradeAndWait` submits the upgrade and then polls that task until it settles: `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED` and `RUNNING` are nonterminal, `SUCCEEDED` is success, `FAILED` and `CANCELED` return `*TaskFailedError` carrying the task, and any status outside the pinned `TaskStatus` enum is a `*ProtocolError`. Exceeding the caller's timeout returns an error wrapping `ErrPollTimeout`, and a cancelled context stops the wait.

Return `*APIError` for any response whose status is not the expected one, populating `StatusCode`, `Code`, `ReferenceID` and `Message` from the `ErrorResponse` body when the service sent one, and `*ProtocolError` for a success response that is not a usable `Task`. `Client` must be safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines.

Give the package its own table-driven tests under `sddclcm/`, driving each case through `t.Run`. Run `bash .moonshiner/verify.sh`; the verifier uses only an in-process contract fixture and the whole module must pass `go test -race`.
